title: DNS tools: dig, getent, resolvectl
summary: Read a dig answer part by part, see what programs really get, and find which DNS servers your machine asks.

text: dig asks DNS directly and shows the whole answer.
- status: NOERROR means it worked. NXDOMAIN: no such name. SERVFAIL: the lookup broke.
- ANSWER holds the records, SERVER says who answered.

scheme: $ dig AAAA example.org      its IPv6 addresses
$ dig MX example.org        its mail servers
text: - Put the record type before the name to ask for it.
- @server asks a given resolver: compare two answers when one looks wrong.
dig only asks DNS. Programs (ping, curl, your app) go through the C library, which reads /etc/hosts first.
- getent hosts shows what programs will really get.
- When dig and your app disagree, look at /etc/hosts.
- With systemd-resolved, dig asks 127.0.0.53, which reads /etc/hosts too: dig @192.168.1.1 skips it.
Many systems run systemd-resolved: programs ask a local stub at 127.0.0.53, which caches and forwards to the real servers.
- resolvectl status lists the real servers, per interface (a VPN can bring its own).
- No systemd-resolved? The real servers are in /etc/resolv.conf itself.
